# MM-P3-L4-SB03-S2 Fastener inspection and torque - Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P3, line P3-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L4-SB03  
Related: ECN-2026-026, MM-P3-L4-SB03, SB-1019

Scope
- This document establishes the approved process for inspection, cleaning, lubrication, and torque verification of fasteners on Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03). 
- It covers structural fasteners, access panel fasteners, and selected machine-mounted hardware that affect containment, alignment, and operator safety. 
- For electrical enclosures and components, follow the applicable procedures referenced in ECN-2026-026 and MM-P3-L4-SB03.

Background and rationale
- Fasteners on shot blast cabinets are exposed to abrasive media, dust loading, and vibration. Over time they can loosen, seize, or corrode, compromising containment and mechanical alignments. 
- Proper inspection and controlled torque application preserve cabinet integrity, reduce unplanned downtime, and maintain safe dust handling performance.
- The dust collector pressure drop alarm for Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03) is 1510 Pa. Maintaining fastener integrity helps ensure seals and access interfaces do not contribute to premature alarm condition.

Tools and consumables
- Torque wrench suitable for specified fastener torque ranges referenced in design documents and manufacturer data. Calibrate per plant calibration policy. 
- Non-marring pry tool for panel extraction. 
- Cleaning brushes and lint-free rags. 
- Penetrating lubricant and anti-seize materials compatible with substrate; use lubricant part number CFW-LUB-526 for general fastener lubrication on EQ-P3-L4-SB03. 
- Torque indicator tags and tamper-evident seals for post-torque marking. 
- Personal protective equipment per SB-1019 and site safety rules.

Procedure
- Pre-work verification
  - Confirm authorization to work on EQ-P3-L4-SB03 and review lockout/tagout requirements in SB-1019.
  - Notify operations and log the planned work in the maintenance schedule and equipment history records referenced in MM-P3-L4-SB03.

- Visual inspection and preparation
  - Visually inspect all exposed fasteners on cabinet panels, access doors, and mounting brackets. Look for signs of back-off, rounding, corrosion, material build-up, or evidence of previous rework.
  - Clean the fastener and surrounding seating surface of abrasive media and dust using brushes and lint-free cloths to ensure accurate torque.
  - Where threads are contaminated or corroded, apply an appropriate penetrating lubricant, then clean again to remove loosened debris. Use lubricant part number CFW-LUB-526 for routine lubrication as it is approved for EQ-P3-L4-SB03.

- Fastener removal where required
  - If removal is necessary for inspection of seating surfaces or hardware condition, label each fastener and matcher point to maintain assembly orientation. Preserve thread engagement features and inspect washers, lock devices, and captive inserts.

- Torque verification and application
  - Refer to the fastener torque specification tables held in ECN-2026-026 and the equipment assembly records in MM-P3-L4-SB03 for the correct torque values for each fastener type. Do not apply a torque value unless it is confirmed in those documents or by the component manufacturer.
  - Use a calibrated torque wrench. Apply torque in a controlled pattern appropriate to the fastener grouping (for example, opposing sequence for panel bolts) to assure uniform seating. Mark each fastener with a torque indicator tag or tamper-evident seal after verification.
  - Document any deviation from specified torque values and the rationale in the maintenance record. If a fastener is found to be damaged or fails to hold torque, replace it and record the replacement per the parts control process.

- Post-assembly checks
  - Confirm panel gaps and seal compression conform to the cabinet assembly condition recorded in MM-P3-L4-SB03.
  - Perform a functional check of the dust collection interface and observe for immediate changes in pressure drop or alarm behavior. Log findings and any corrective actions taken.

Examples and judgement notes
- Example: if an access door fastener shows rounding of the head but the seating surface is intact, replace the fastener and, after replacement, confirm torque value from ECN-2026-026 before final tightening. Tag the new fastener and note the part used in the records.
- Example: where a captive stud exhibits surface corrosion confined to the outside diameter, clean and coat with CFW-LUB-526 then verify retained torque per the specification table. If threads are compromised, replace the stud assembly.

Acceptance criteria
- All inspected fasteners show no evidence of progressive loosening at re-inspection and pass the torque verification to the values specified in ECN-2026-026 and MM-P3-L4-SB03.
- Access panels and sealing interfaces exhibit consistent seating and no visible gaps affecting containment. Where applicable, no new dust ingress pathways are observed.
- Lubrication is applied using lubricant part number CFW-LUB-526 where specified and documented.
- Any replacement hardware is recorded with the part description and associated justification in the maintenance log.

Records to keep
- Maintenance work order and completion report filed in the equipment history for EQ-P3-L4-SB03 per MM-P3-L4-SB03.
- Torque verification checklist including torque wrench calibration reference, operator name, date, and fastener identifiers. Retain with the preventive maintenance record.
- Any deviation reports and corrective action records referenced to ECN-2026-026 when changes to hardware or torque values are proposed.
- Safety and LOTO confirmation form per SB-1019.

References
- ECN-2026-026
- MM-P3-L4-SB03
- SB-1019

Notes
- This procedure does not provide specific torque values. Use the authoritative specification documents cited above for numeric torque values and any changes to fastener selection or torque practice.
